mcqs.question: Two students calculate the median of the same grouped data (class intervals 10‑20, 20‑30, 30‑40, 40‑50 with frequencies 5, 8, 12, 5). Student A uses the class limits directly as the lower limit L, while Student B first converts the limits to class boundaries (9.5‑20.5, 20.5‑30.5, 30.5‑40.5, 40.5‑50.5) and then applies the median formula. Which statement correctly describes the effect of substituting class boundaries correctly?

options.A: Both students obtain exactly the same median value.
options.B: Student B’s median will be higher than Student A’s median.
options.C: Student A’s median will be higher than Student B’s median.
options.D: Neither method can be used for grouped data.

mcqs.answer: Student B’s median will be higher than Student A’s median.
mcqs.explanation: Using class boundaries shifts the lower limit of the median class from 30 to 30.5 while the class width remains 10. The median formula L + [(N/2 – cf_prev)/f]·h therefore yields a larger value when the correct boundaries are used. Hence Student B, who uses boundaries, obtains a higher median (32.17) than Student A (31.67). Options A, C and D are incorrect because the two methods give different results, Student B’s result is the higher one, and the formula is valid for grouped data.

mcqs.question: In a class of 40 students, the marks are grouped and the median of the grouped data is found to be 68. Which of the following statements correctly interprets this median?

options.A: At least half of the students scored more than 68 marks.
options.B: Exactly half of the students scored more than 68 marks.
options.C: Half of the total frequency lies below 68 and the other half lies above 68.
options.D: 68 is the mean (average) of the marks.

mcqs.answer: Half of the total frequency lies below 68 and the other half lies above 68.
mcqs.explanation: The median of grouped data is the value that divides the total frequency into two equal parts. Therefore, 50 % of the cumulative frequency is below the median and 50 % is above it. Option C states this definition precisely. Option A is too strong ("at least half"), Option B is false because the median does not guarantee exactly half the individual scores are above it, and Option D confuses median with mean.

mcqs.question:
For the grouped data below, what is the cumulative frequency up to the class 20‑30?
Class intervals: 0‑10 | 10‑20 | 20‑30
Frequencies: 4 | 7 | 9
mcqs.explanation: Cumulative frequency is obtained by adding frequencies of all classes up to the required class. 4 + 7 + 9 = 20. Hence option B is correct. The other options represent partial sums or a single class frequency.

mcqs.question:
The following grouped data represent the number of books read by students.
Class intervals: 0‑5 | 5‑10 | 10‑15 | 15‑20
Frequencies: 3 | 7 | 12 | 5
Which class is the median class?
mcqs.explanation: Total frequency N = 3 + 7 + 12 + 5 = 27. Half of N is 13.5. Cumulative frequencies are 3, 10, 22, 27. The first cumulative frequency that exceeds 13.5 is 22, which belongs to the class 10‑15. Therefore, 10‑15 is the median class. Options A, B and D are incorrect because their cumulative frequencies are below N/2.

mcqs.question: Which of the following expressions correctly represents the formula for the median of grouped data?
mcqs.explanation:
The standard formula for the median of grouped data is:
Median = L + [(N/2 – cf_prev) / f] × h,
where L = lower class boundary of the median class, N = total frequency, cf_prev = cumulative frequency before the median class, f = frequency of the median class, and h = class width. Option A matches this formula exactly. The other options either omit the N/2 term or use incorrect operations.

mcqs.question: A grouped frequency distribution has the class 20‑30 with frequency 15. The class boundaries are 19.5 and 30.5, the total frequency N = 50 and the cumulative frequency before this class is 22. Using the correct class boundaries, what is the median of the data?
mcqs.explanation:
First compute N/2 = 25. Apply the median formula:
L = 19.5 (lower boundary), h = 30.5 – 19.5 = 11,
cf_prev = 22, f = 15.
Median = 19.5 + [(25 – 22) / 15] × 11 = 19.5 + (3/15) × 11 = 19.5 + 0.2 × 11 = 19.5 + 2.2 = 21.7.
Thus option A is correct. The other options arise from using wrong limits or forgetting to convert to boundaries.

mcqs.question: In a company, the salaries of employees are grouped and the median salary is found to be Rs 45,000. Which interpretation is correct?

options.A: Rs 45,000 is the average (mean) salary of all employees.
options.B: Rs 45,000 is the most frequently occurring salary.
options.C: 50 % of the employees earn less than Rs 45,000 and 50 % earn more than Rs 45,000.

mcqs.answer: 50 % of the employees earn less than Rs 45,000 and 50 % earn more than Rs 45,000.
mcqs.explanation: The median divides the data into two equal halves. Therefore, half of the total cumulative frequency lies below the median value and the other half lies above it. Option C states this property. Option A confuses median with mean, Option B confuses it with mode, and Option D is not necessarily true; the median can coincide with an actual salary.

mcqs.question:
A survey records the ages of participants in the following grouped form:
0‑10 years: 5 people
10‑20 years: 12 people
20‑30 years: 9 people
30‑40 years: 4 people
What is the cumulative frequency up to the class 20‑30 years?
mcqs.explanation: Cumulative frequency up to a class is the sum of frequencies of all preceding classes including the class itself. 5 + 12 + 9 = 26. Hence option B is correct. Option A omits the 0‑10 class, Option C adds only two classes, and Option D is just the frequency of the 10‑20 class.
